input_messages.content: Hi, I’m having trouble with my mobile data. The internet on my phone is either extremely slow or just stops working altogether. I really need to get excellent internet speed—nothing less will do. I don’t have access to Wi-Fi, so I need this fixed as soon as possible. Can you help?
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. Let me know what you need me to do next to get this fixed.
I tried running a speed test, but it failed due to no connection. My mobile data just isn’t working at all right now. What should I do next?

Looking at my status bar, I see that I have excellent signal strength and 5G is showing, but there’s also an icon that says “Data Disabled.” I don’t see Airplane Mode or “No Signal.” What should I do next?
I turned mobile data back on, but when I tried the speed test again, it still failed due to no connection. What should I try next?
I checked my SIM card status, and it’s showing as active and working. What should I do next to get my mobile data working?

I checked my APN settings. The APN name is set to “internet” and the MMSC URL is “http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc.” Do these look correct, or should I go ahead and reset the APN settings to default?

Yes, let’s go ahead and reset the APN settings to default. Please let me know what steps I should follow, or if you can do it from your end, go ahead. I’ll reboot my device after the reset as you suggested.

I reset the APN settings to default and rebooted my device, but the speed test still fails due to no connection. This is getting frustrating—what else can we try to get my mobile data working with excellent speed?
I checked, and Data Saver mode is already turned off on my phone. What should I try next to get my mobile data working at excellent speed?
I definitely don’t want to change my plan, but I’m willing to refuel 2GB of data so I can get excellent internet speed again. Please go ahead and add 2GB to my account and let me know once it’s done.
It looks like there isn’t a payment request for the data refuel yet. Could you please send the payment request for 2GB of data so I can proceed? I want to get this resolved as soon as possible.

I rebooted my device after the data refuel, but the speed test still fails due to no connection. My mobile data still isn’t working at all, and I really need excellent internet speed. What else can we try?

Here’s what I found:
1. VPN is currently enabled and connected.
2. My network mode preference is set to 4G/5G preferred.
3. The only icons in my status bar are 5G, excellent signal, data enabled, and VPN connected—no unusual warnings.

Should I try disconnecting the VPN to see if that helps?
I disconnected the VPN and tried the speed test again, but it still fails due to no connection. My mobile data is still not working at all. What else can we try to get excellent internet speed?

I’m not interested in changing my plan—I only want my current plan to work with excellent internet speed, as promised. I’ve already refueled 2GB of data, so I should have access to mobile data now. Is there anything else you can do to restore my connection and get me excellent speed without changing my plan?

instructions.task_instructions:
If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved only when speed test returns excellent internet speed and nothing else. If it returns poor, fair or good, you will not consider the issue resolved. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

Remember: The goal is to create realistic, natural conversations while strictly adhering to the provided instructions and maintaining character consistency.

messages.content: Hi! How can I help you today?

Hi, I’m having trouble with my mobile data. The internet on my phone is either extremely slow or just stops working altogether. I really need to get excellent internet speed—nothing less will do. I don’t have access to Wi-Fi, so I need this fixed as soon as possible. Can you help?

To assist you with your mobile data issue, I’ll need to identify your account first. Could you please provide one of the following:
- The phone number associated with your account,
- Your full name and date of birth,
- Or your customer ID?

Once I have this information, I can begin troubleshooting your mobile data problem.
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. Let me know what you need me to do next to get this fixed.

Thank you for providing your information. To begin troubleshooting your mobile data issue, I’ll need you to perform a quick speed test on your phone. This will help determine the current quality of your mobile data connection.

Please run a speed test on your device and let me know the result. If you need instructions on how to do this, just let me know your phone type (Android or iPhone), and I can guide you through the steps.
Speed test failed: No Connection.
I tried running a speed test, but it failed due to no connection. My mobile data just isn’t working at all right now. What should I do next?

Thank you for letting me know. Since your speed test failed due to no connection, let’s start by checking your phone’s basic connectivity status. 

Please check your phone’s status bar and let me know:
- If you see any signal bars (and how many)
- If you see any icons like “Airplane Mode,” “No Signal,” or “Data Disabled”

This will help determine if the issue is with your cellular service, mobile data settings, or something else. If you need instructions on how to check your status bar, let me know your phone type.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔒 VPN Connected | 🔋 80%

Looking at my status bar, I see that I have excellent signal strength and 5G is showing, but there’s also an icon that says “Data Disabled.” I don’t see Airplane Mode or “No Signal.” What should I do next?

Your phone is showing “Data Disabled,” which means mobile data is currently turned off. To restore your internet connection, please enable mobile data on your device.

On most phones, you can do this by:
- Swiping down from the top of your screen to open the quick settings panel.
- Looking for the “Mobile Data” or “Cellular Data” icon.
- Tapping it to turn it ON.

Once you’ve enabled mobile data, try running the speed test again and let me know the result. If you need step-by-step instructions for your specific phone type, please let me know if you’re using Android or iPhone.

Mobile Data is now ON.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔒 VPN Connected | 🔋 80%
Speed test failed: No Connection.
I turned mobile data back on, but when I tried the speed test again, it still failed due to no connection. What should I try next?

Thank you for updating me. Since mobile data is now enabled but you still have no connection, let’s check if there are any issues with your SIM card, as this can affect your ability to connect to the network.

Please check your SIM card status on your phone. On most devices, you can do this by going to:
- Settings > About Phone > Status > SIM Status (Android)
- Settings > Cellular > SIM Applications (iPhone)

Let me know if your SIM card is listed as “Active,” “Missing,” or “Locked.” If you need help finding this setting, let me know your phone type.
Your SIM card is active and working.
I checked my SIM card status, and it’s showing as active and working. What should I do next to get my mobile data working?

Since your SIM card is active and working, the next step is to check your phone’s APN (Access Point Name) settings. Incorrect APN settings can prevent your mobile data from working even if you have signal and an active SIM.

Please check your APN settings on your phone:
- On Android: Settings > Network & Internet > Mobile Network > Access Point Names
- On iPhone: Settings > Cellular > Cellular Data Network

Look for the APN name and MMSC URL. If you see anything unusual or if you’re unsure, let me know what’s listed there. If you’d like, I can guide you through resetting your APN settings to default, which often resolves mobile data issues. Would you like to proceed with resetting your APN settings?

Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)

I checked my APN settings. The APN name is set to “internet” and the MMSC URL is “http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc.” Do these look correct, or should I go ahead and reset the APN settings to default?

Your APN name and MMSC URL appear to be standard, but sometimes resetting the APN settings to default can resolve hidden configuration issues.

Would you like to proceed with resetting your APN settings to default? If you do, please confirm, and I’ll guide you through the process. After resetting, you’ll need to reboot your device for the changes to take effect.

Yes, let’s go ahead and reset the APN settings to default. Please let me know what steps I should follow, or if you can do it from your end, go ahead. I’ll reboot my device after the reset as you suggested.

I’m unable to reset the APN settings directly from my end, but I can guide you through the process. Please follow these steps to reset your APN settings to default:

For Android:
1. Go to Settings > Network & Internet > Mobile Network > Access Point Names.
2. Tap the three dots (menu) in the upper right corner.
3. Select “Reset to default.”

For iPhone:
1. Go to Settings > Cellular > Cellular Data Network.
2. Scroll to the bottom and tap “Reset Settings.”

After you reset the APN settings, please reboot your device. Once your phone restarts, try running the speed test again and let me know if your mobile data is working.

APN settings will reset at reboot.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔒 VPN Connected | 🔋 80%

Resetting APN settings...
Restarting network services...
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔒 VPN Connected | 🔋 80%
Speed test failed: No Connection.

I reset the APN settings to default and rebooted my device, but the speed test still fails due to no connection. This is getting frustrating—what else can we try to get my mobile data working with excellent speed?

Thank you for your patience. Since resetting the APN settings and rebooting did not resolve the issue, let’s check if there are any restrictions or settings on your device that might be blocking mobile data.

Please check if Data Saver mode is enabled on your phone. Data Saver can restrict background data and sometimes interfere with connectivity.

On Android:
- Go to Settings > Network & Internet > Data Saver.
- Make sure Data Saver is turned OFF.

On iPhone:
- Go to Settings > Cellular > Cellular Data Options > Low Data Mode.
- Make sure Low Data Mode is turned OFF.

Please let me know if Data Saver or Low Data Mode is enabled, and turn it off if it is. After making this change, try the speed test again and let me know the result.
Data Saver mode is OFF.
I checked, and Data Saver mode is already turned off on my phone. What should I try next to get my mobile data working at excellent speed?
